The good country folks win and the bad city folks are chased off ... but even the bad guys (banker, modern artist) aren't really all that bad. Agree with other commenters on the incongruity of period. Feels like 1936, and none of the cars or radios are newer than 1936. But the hairstyles are definitely '41, so it was most likely made then.

Zasu Pitts (she pronounced it "Say-zoo") plays the same character beloved of audiences for decades. However, she also was a fine actor who occasionally was given the chance to prove it. Gale Storm is also delightful here as the young girl visiting the country and her peculiar Uncle Joe. Not really a single character here to dislike. Even the banker trying to foreclose on Zasu gets twisted around by her character's logical twists and turns. A very relaxing and enjoyable hour!
Delightful and entertaining little film. Many thanks for supplying the Zasu Pitts fix!
